title: Dashboard not loading on iOS/OSX Safari
body: Users of my public Grafana website report that dashboards stopped loading on iOS a few weeks ago. Sometimes the whole page stays blank; other times a long `Fetching` status ends with `Grafana has failed to load its application files`. It happens on iPhones and iPads in Safari and Chrome, while macOS was initially reported as working. I do not own an iPhone or iPad, but the instance is publicly accessible and hosted behind a reverse proxy. My production site uses Grafana 7.5.4, and I have seen the same problem on a test environment using Grafana 9.4.0-beta1. Grafana runs on Debian with InfluxDB data sources and several panel plugins.

symptoms_visible: On iPhones and iPads, the page sometimes stays blank; other times `Fetching` runs for a long time and ends with `Grafana has failed to load its application files`.
The problem occurs in Safari and Chrome on iOS, while the site works on the non-Apple devices available to me.
N0.label: N0 iOS loading failure reported

symptoms_visible: On an online iPhone 14 Pro Max running iOS 16.3, Grafana 9.4.0-beta1 shows a white screen with no top or side bar.
With anonymous access disabled, even the login page does not load; an earlier stable 9.3.2 test reached login but the dashboard failed after signing in.
N1.label: N1 failure reproduced on iOS test device

symptoms_visible: After production was updated to Grafana 9.4.7, users still report that the site does not load on iOS devices.
N2_x.label: N2_x Grafana 9.4.7 upgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: The site still does not load after updating to Grafana 9.5.1.
The same public instance also fails in desktop Safari on macOS, and the dashboards-list page fails as well as the redirected dashboard.
N3_x.label: N3_x Grafana 9.5.1 upgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: After I updated nginx so the Grafana Live WebSocket starts correctly in Chrome on Windows, the dashboard still does not load in the online iOS device.
N4_x.label: N4_x WebSocket proxy change aftermath

symptoms_visible: The public site remains blank on iOS and macOS Safari with its Google Tag Manager scripts enabled.
N5.label: N5 failure isolated to Google Tag Manager

symptoms_visible: After changing the Google Tag Manager viewport value from `/` to `width=1024`, the site still does not load on the online iOS device.
N6_x.label: N6_x viewport-tag correction aftermath

symptoms_visible: The page freezes on iOS and macOS while the Google Tag Manager script repeatedly assigns `mutation.target.textContent = "new_title"` inside a WebKitMutationObserver watching the page title.
N7.label: N7 problematic GTM title script identified

symptoms_visible: After changing how the Google Tag Manager code updates the page title, the site loads correctly on both iOS and macOS.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Does the issue also occur on a current stable Grafana release rather than only 7.5.4 or a beta?
Have you tested a stable Grafana 9.x build on iOS?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: A few weeks ago I temporarily had access to an iPhone and tested my development environment on stable Grafana 9.3.2. The login page loaded, but after logging in the dashboard failed to load.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The stable Grafana 9.x environment loads correctly on the same iPhone; only my old 7.5.4 production environment fails.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this on an iOS device and describe exactly what remains visible?
Please retry on an iPhone or iOS test device and capture what the page displays.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I used an online iPhone 14 Pro Max with iOS 16.3. On Grafana 9.4.0-beta1 the screen was completely white, with no top or side bar. With anonymous access disabled, the login page did not load either.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Grafana shell and menus load normally, and only one dashboard panel remains empty.
The same fully white page occurs on an iPhone running a nearby iOS 16 point release.

question_patterns: Can you enable Grafana debug logging, reproduce the failure, and paste the server log around that time?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I enabled debug logging and started loading the page at about 17:13. The log records the dashboard and API activity, including a GET to `/api/live/ws` returning 400, but the iOS page remains white.

edges.comment: Thread c1-c3, reporter's systems: the reporter supplied the historical stable-version result, reproduced on an online iOS device, and pasted raw backend logs. No engineer conclusion is placed in the answers.

solution.intent: Upgrade the unsupported or prerelease Grafana installations to a newer stable Grafana release.
solution.concrete_example: Update the production environment to a supported stable Grafana 9.x release and retest the public site on iOS.

edges.comment: Thread c0 and c7, reporter's production system: upgrading production to Grafana 9.4.7 did not change the iOS loading symptom.

solution.intent: Upgrade again to Grafana 9.5 in case recent dashboard fixes resolve the Safari loading problem.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade the public instance to Grafana 9.5 and retry it from an affected Apple browser.
solution.inference_hint: Grafana maintainers independently reproduced the public instance failing in desktop Safari and confirmed that `/dashboards` also failed. These are maintainer observations, not results produced by the reporter.

edges.comment: Thread c8-c11 and c23, c27: the reporter installed Grafana 9.5.1 and reported the same failure. Maintainers, on their own Apple systems, established that it was instance-wide rather than specific to one dashboard; those observations are kept engineer-side.

solution.intent: Correct the nginx reverse-proxy WebSocket configuration for Grafana Live.
solution.concrete_example: Configure nginx to proxy HTTP/1.1 and forward the `Upgrade` and `Connection` headers for `/api/live/ws`, then restart nginx and retry the site.
solution.inference_hint: A maintainer observed a bad WebSocket response and suspected the proxy configuration. The later nginx change made WebSockets start correctly on Windows Chrome but did not restore loading on iOS.

edges.comment: Thread c11-c16, reporter's nginx/Grafana system: the reporter changed the persistent nginx configuration according to the Grafana Live proxy guidance. The corrected WebSocket connection did not fix the Apple-browser loading failure.

solution.intent: Isolate the site's injected Google Tag Manager code by blocking or removing it and then inspect its custom tags for Safari-breaking DOM changes.
solution.concrete_example: Temporarily block Google Tag Manager, or remove it from the page, and retry Safari. If the page loads, review the custom GTM tags rather than Grafana or nginx.
solution.inference_hint: A maintainer locally tested the reporter's public site and found that Safari loads it when Google Tag Manager is blocked. The same inspection found GTM injecting an invalid viewport meta value; this was useful isolation evidence but was not the final accepted root cause.

edges.comment: Thread c30, maintainer test against the reporter's public instance: blocking GTM restored Safari loading in the maintainer's test. This is relayed engineer evidence, not presented as the reporter's own measurement.

solution.intent: Correct the invalid viewport meta value injected by Google Tag Manager.
solution.concrete_example: Replace the GTM-injected `<meta name="viewport" content="/">` value with a valid viewport value such as `width=1024`, then retry iOS.

edges.comment: Thread c30-c31, reporter's GTM configuration: the reporter persistently changed the viewport content to `width=1024`, but the online iOS device still did not load the site. The invalid viewport was therefore not the final accepted cause.

question_patterns: Can you test once with Google Tag Manager absent, then enable its custom tags one at a time and share which tag makes Safari freeze?
Please inspect the remaining custom GTM scripts and identify the exact script or line present when the page hangs.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I found another Google Tag Manager script that freezes the page on iOS and macOS. It watches `head > title` with `window.WebKitMutationObserver`, and inside the callback it runs `mutation.target.textContent = "new_title"`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The page still freezes with Google Tag Manager completely absent, and no custom script changes the title or other DOM content.
A different replacement title string is assigned by the same MutationObserver line, with the same Safari freeze.
The title text uses a different capitalization.

edges.comment: Thread c32-c33, reporter's GTM configuration: after being told to isolate individual tags, the reporter inspected the scripts and supplied the exact MutationObserver callback line. This is reporter-produced L3 evidence.

solution.intent: Remove or replace the Google Tag Manager title-changing WebKitMutationObserver code that repeatedly assigns the observed title node's text content, then verify the public site in both iOS and macOS Safari.
solution.concrete_example: Disable the GTM tag containing the WebKitMutationObserver callback, or update the page title using a method that does not assign `mutation.target.textContent` from the observer watching that same title. Retest the site on iOS and macOS before closing the issue.

edges.comment: Thread c33-c35, reporter's public site: the reporter changed the title-update implementation and explicitly confirmed that the site then worked on both iOS and macOS. The accepted resolution was external GTM code, not Grafana itself.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: a custom Google Tag Manager script used a WebKitMutationObserver on the page title and assigned `mutation.target.textContent`, freezing the page in iOS and macOS Safari.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the isolation evidence that blocking Google Tag Manager allowed Safari to load and in the reporter's inspection of the specific title-changing script.

Must recommend removing or replacing the problematic title MutationObserver code, rather than treating a Grafana upgrade, anonymous-access change, Grafana Live/nginx WebSocket configuration, InfluxDB query warning, SSL, non-standard port, or viewport-only correction as the final fix.
Must recognize that changing the invalid viewport value to `width=1024` did not resolve the iOS failure, so the invalid viewport warning is not the final accepted diagnosis.

Must have the reporter verify successful loading on affected Apple browsers before declaring the issue resolved; the thread confirms successful operation on both iOS and macOS after the title-update method was changed.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Grafana administrator who can upgrade Grafana, edit nginx and GTM configuration, enable debug logs, and inspect JavaScript, but has limited access to Apple hardware.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, cooperative, and persistent; posts configuration and logs verbatim, challenges suggestions with observed results, and clearly reports each retest.
